physical_harm: Death of two persons and injuries to two
key_evidence_accepted: The prosecution relied on the statements of injured witnesses PW-3 and PW-4, and the post-mortem report corroborating stab wounds on the deceased. The court accepted that the appellants were armed with spears and other weapons, while the deceased were not armed.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the injured witnesses PW-3 and PW-4 as credible, as their statements led to the lodging of the First Information Report and were corroborated by the post-mortem report.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 1st July 1987; Trial judgment: 24.10.2008; High Court and Supreme Court decisions: 24.10.2008, April 23, 2019
legal_representation: Ravi Prakash Mehrotra, Ankit Agarwal, Ms. Deepti R. Mehrotra, Advs. for the Appellants; Ms. Jesal Wahi (for Ms. Hemantika Wahi), Adv. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR lodged on 2nd July 1987; cross-case registered; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Sections 302 and 324 IPC; High Court: Maintained conviction; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution has relied upon the statement of complainant PW-3 as also the statement of PW-4 who are injured witnesses. PW-2, the doctor has been examined to prove the injuries on prosecution witnesses. The appellants were having spear, accused was having axe and other were having sticks. They attacked the deceased and both the injured witnesses with spears and axe.
defence_argument: The appellants have lodged cross First Information Report. They argue that the deceased and their accomplices, 9 in number, were the aggressors. The injuries have been inflicted on both the appellants. Such injuries have been proved by PW-10, Dr. Nikhilkumar Buch. The appellants have received grievous injuries, while protecting the possession of their land, thus, they have acted in their right of private defence. They also argue that the occurrence has taken place at the spur of the moment without any pre-meditation and that the appellants are not taken any advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
legal_principle_applied: The right of private defence is to protect the person and the property. In such right, the person cannot cause more harm than what is necessary for the protection of the person and the property. The right of private defence is not available when the alleged assailants are unarmed.
precedent_relied_upon: Jangir Singh v. State of Punjab 2018 (15) SCALE 88
sentencing_rationale: The Trial Court as well as the High Court was perfectly justified in law in convicting and sentencing the appellants for the offence under Section 302 IPC. The deceased had multiple stab wounds on the chest. Since there are multiple wounds, it cannot be said that the appellants have acted at the spur of the moment without pre-meditation and that the appellants have not taken any advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.
